title: Rain, snow and dust in Rust: the engine's soft round particles around the camera, never cubes
note: Rain, snow and dust are Particles::rain, ::snow and ::dust made once in on_reset and drawn with frame.particles: soft round dots, never meshes.
intent: Snowflakes, raindrops and dust motes drawn as tiny cube meshes read as flying blocks. Use the engine's particles (docs/api/particles.md): Particles::snow(top, half_extent) drops soft round flakes 2.5 cm across at 1 m/s from a box's top, settling briefly where they land; Particles::rain(top, half_extent) draws streaks that stop on what the camera sees; Particles::dust(origin, half_extent) hangs faint 5 mm motes throughout a box, unlit, so make the box the sunbeam. Make each emitter once in on_reset, keep it in the world and draw it every frame with frame.particles(&emitter). An emitter is its description: with_origin(..) at a new place each frame makes a new one, and the renderer holds only 16, so never move a box with the camera. Cover the world with a few rain or snow boxes made once instead and draw those near the camera. Tune with .with_rate(per_tick, lifetime_ticks) or .with_look(..) rather than more emitters; a phone draws every n-th particle past its cap.
port: The world's owner (or a weather facet) makes and draws the emitters; no other facet draws weather or dust, and none draws them as meshes.

evidence.note: Particles::snow, ::rain and ::dust, frame.particles, an emitter made once and the renderer's 16.
